case_assessment.summary: The graph captures the basic accident path from vessel rupture to BLEVE, but it misses the report's central physical degradation step, uses a weak treatment of confinement, and includes one schema-compliance problem in the hazard evidence. The initiating event is also modeled a bit too narrowly as only the observed leak.
main_problems: The main physical cause identified in the report—severe corrosion thinning of the SCR bottom head—is missing.
High confinement is not directly linked to the BLEVE, even though the report identifies containment as one of the required BLEVE components.
The edge from High confinement to High pressure is a weak abstraction and is less informative than linking confinement directly to the BLEVE.
H1 uses paraphrased evidence instead of a short direct quote from the incident text.
Ev1 is framed only as a leak observation, but the immediate sequence also involved continued operation and startup of the leaking vessel.

node_updates.current_state: Evidence is a paraphrased multi-sentence summary and not a direct quote from the report.
node_updates.suggested_state: Use a direct quote such as: "the pressure vessel failure caused a boiling liquid expanding vapor explosion (BLEVE)"
node_updates.reason: The schema requires a short verbatim quote when support is available. The current evidence is not schema-compliant even though direct supporting text exists.
node_updates.evidence: the pressure vessel failure caused a boiling liquid expanding vapor explosion (BLEVE)

node_updates.current_state: InitiatingEvent is modeled only as "Leak from underneath the SCR".
node_updates.suggested_state: Clarify Ev1 as the leaking SCR remaining in service and being restarted during normal startup, rather than leak discovery alone.
node_updates.reason: The leak was the first abnormal sign, but the report's immediate sequence includes continued operation of the leaking vessel and restart on April 3 before final rupture.
node_updates.evidence: Loy-Lange continued operating the leaking pressure vessel throughout the remainder of the Friday production schedule ... The following Monday a Loy-Lange stationary engineer began his normal start-up routine at about 6:00 a.m. At around 7:20 a.m. on April 3, 2017, the SCR bottom head catastrophically failed.

node_additions.suggested_name: Severe corrosion thinning of the SCR bottom head
node_additions.reason: This is the main physical degradation mechanism identified by the report. Without it, the graph jumps from a leak to catastrophic failure and omits the core equipment-integrity cause of the rupture.
node_additions.evidence: Oxygen pitting corrosion and generalized corrosion thinned the pressure vessel bottom head until it could no longer contain the pressure inside the vessel.

edge_additions.reason: Containment/high confinement is one of the explicitly stated prerequisites for a BLEVE and should be linked directly to the hazard consequence.
edge_additions.evidence: A BLEVE requires three components: 1) a liquid that exists above its normal atmospheric pressure boiling point; 2) containment that causes the pressure on the liquid to be sufficiently high to suppress boiling; and, 3) a sudden loss of containment to rapidly drop the pressure on the liquid

edge_deletions.reason: This is a weaker and less useful intermediate abstraction than linking confinement directly to the BLEVE. In this graph, confinement and high pressure are better represented as parallel enabling conditions for the hazard consequence.
edge_deletions.evidence: A BLEVE requires three components: 1) a liquid that exists above its normal atmospheric pressure boiling point; 2) containment that causes the pressure on the liquid to be sufficiently high to suppress boiling; and, 3) a sudden loss of containment to rapidly drop the pressure on the liquid

issues_summary.description: The graph omits severe corrosion thinning of the SCR bottom head, which the report identifies as the main physical cause of rupture.
The confinement-to-pressure edge is weaker than modeling confinement as a direct BLEVE prerequisite.
High confinement is not directly connected to the BLEVE even though the report explicitly lists containment as one of the required BLEVE components.
H1 evidence is paraphrased rather than quoted verbatim from the incident description.
The initiating event is modeled too narrowly as only leak observation and under-represents continued operation and startup of the leaking vessel before rupture.
